roll.overlap: Overlapping notes of the same pitch and channel export on separate event tracks, preserving their timings and channel. MIDI 1.0 receivers may play these overlaps differently; review playback in the target instrument.
roll.saveBoundary: Saving creates a separate user-edited score. Original model predictions and generated candidates stay unchanged; temporary audio imports remain temporary.
roll.help: Draw on empty space to add; drag a note to move, its right edge to resize. Ctrl-click toggles selection; Shift-drag draws a selection box. Right-click deletes only that note. Ctrl+C/V, Ctrl+Z/Y and Delete work when the editor is focused.
roll.invalid: Invalid note value. The current score was preserved; correct the value and try again.
roll.bends: Pitch bends stay on their original part timeline; moving one note does not silently rewrite shared bend events.
roll.octave: Octave labels use C4 = MIDI 60. MIDI note numbers are authoritative.

ux04.noModelGeneration: Model generation and recomposition have not qualified for this runtime and remain unavailable. Rule composition does not recognize style or copy a reference melody.

composerHelp.tempo: 20–300 beats per minute. Changes playback speed, not the number of generated notes.
composerHelp.key: Choose the root pitch. With other settings fixed, changes melody and chord pitches; for example C or D.
composerHelp.scale: Major and natural minor change the allowed scale tones, without classifying mood.
composerHelp.bars: Length: 1–32 bars. The meter determines beats per bar.
composerHelp.density: 0.1–1 controls retention probability at noninitial positions; higher values generally keep more notes. Bar starts remain. Counts are not guaranteed to increase for every seed.
composerHelp.rhythm: Even uses 1-beat candidate steps; syncopated uses 0.5-beat steps. Density and activity still govern retention.
composerHelp.seed: Integer 0–4294967295. Same algorithm version, settings and seed reproduce the same result. A different seed changes random choices.
composerHelp.meter: For example 4/4, 3/4 or 6/8. In this score contract, 6/8 means three quarter-note beats per bar.
composerHelp.progression: Space-separated Roman degrees I–VII, case insensitive. Example: I vi IV V. Letter case does not independently specify chord quality; triads use the selected scale.
composerHelp.energyCurve: 1–32 numbers from 0 to 1, separated by spaces and assigned across bars. Affects note retention and velocity, not audio RMS. Example: 0.4 0.7 0.8 0.5.
composerHelp.style: Intent notes only. The current rule engine does not use this text to generate a musical style.

analysisStates.SOURCE_MISSING: Original audio missing; historical analysis retained

ux04.bindingPending: Checking the analysis version and audio identity. No unverified values are displayed.
ux04.fragmentBoundary: These results describe the selected interval, up to 30 seconds. They do not describe the entire song.
ux04.ruleBoundary: Deterministic rule draft · RULE_BASED_DRAFT. This is not music understanding or style recognition.
ux04.notesBoundary: Your notes are saved separately as user edits; the original machine analysis remains unchanged.
ux04.notesPlaceholder: Record what you hear, favorite sounds, arrangement ideas or passages worth referencing.
ux04.chartHover: Move over the chart, or focus it and use arrow keys, to read a sample.
ux04.omarPurpose: Convert audio to features suited to computer comparison and retrieval. Future reference comparison is not implemented here; this does not recognize genre, mood or style.
ux04.noFeatures: No features for the current audio yet

metricHelp.bpmCandidates: An algorithm estimate, not a confirmed song tempo.
metricHelp.beats: Estimated beat positions within this interval.
metricHelp.onsets: Estimated sound-start positions; not a count of separate instruments.
metricHelp.rms: Native PCM mean-square amplitude over this interval and all channels. Not LUFS.
metricHelp.samplePeak: Largest absolute native PCM sample, relative to full scale 1.
metricHelp.crestFactor: Sample peak divided by RMS; not dynamic range or loudness range.
metricHelp.spectralCentroid: Frequency-weighted spectral center, in Hz; cannot identify an instrument.
metricHelp.spectralFlux: Positive change between normalized spectral frames; not confirmed section boundaries.
metricHelp.tonalCandidates: Prominent pitch classes estimated from chroma, not confirmed keys.
metricHelp.lufs: No qualified loudness measurement is available; no value is inferred.

chartHelp.energy: RMS amplitude of resampled mono frames. This differs from the all-channel window RMS card and is not perceptual loudness.
chartHelp.spectralCentroid: Frequency-weighted center of each spectral frame; higher values do not prove a specific instrument.
chartHelp.spectralFlux: Positive spectral-frame difference. Peaks show measured spectral changes, not verse or chorus boundaries.

rules.energyHigher: The average displayed RMS samples in the second half ({{back}}) exceed those in the first half ({{front}}).
rules.energyLower: The average displayed RMS samples in the second half ({{back}}) are below those in the first half ({{front}}).
rules.energySimilar: The two half-interval RMS sample averages are within 10%: {{front}} and {{back}}.
rules.fluxMaximum: The largest published spectral-change sample is at {{time}} s, with value {{value}}.
rules.onsetRate: There are {{count}} onset candidates, averaging {{rate}} per second in this interval.
